q: Can I claim a carbon credit for selling or recycling my production scrap?
title: Carbon credit for selling scrap?
short: No. Selling or recycling your scrap does not earn a carbon credit and cannot be subtracted from your footprint. Under the GHG Protocol, you report only the emissions of getting scrap to the recycler, and any benefit of recycling goes to the user of the recycled material. Avoided emissions may be reported separately.
audience: Metal, plastic and paper converters in India

sections.h: Why there is no credit in your inventory
p: The GHG Protocol Corporate Standard keeps your inventory to emissions that happen, and says avoided emissions must be reported separately, never netted off. The Scope 3 Standard applies the same logic to waste in Category 5: for recycled waste, the generator counts transport to the recycling point and any handling before it; the recycling process itself belongs to whoever buys and uses the recycled material.
This stops the same reduction being claimed twice, once by you for sending scrap and again by the buyer for using recycled content.

sections.h: Why it is not a carbon credit either
p: A carbon credit comes from a registered project under an approved methodology, with additionality and third-party verification, issued by a programme such as Verra or Gold Standard. Selling scrap to a dealer is normal business that would happen anyway, so it does not meet those tests. A recycler running a registered project may earn credits, but those are theirs.

sections.h: Related schemes that are not carbon credits
ul: Plastic EPR certificates in India are generated by registered recyclers on the CPCB portal for producers' recycling obligations. They are a compliance instrument for plastic, not tonnes of CO2.
Scrap revenue reduces your product cost, not your emissions.
Lower scrap rates do cut emissions, because less material is bought and processed per good unit.

ol: Category 5: the transport of scrap to the dealer or recycler, if you arrange or pay for it, and any treatment before the recycling point.
A separate note on avoided emissions from recycling, with method and source, clearly outside your Scope 1, 2 and 3 totals.
In a product footprint under ISO 14067, state whether you use a cut-off or an end-of-life approach. With cut-off, recycling benefits go to the material's next user.

senseible: Senseible does not calculate recycling credits or avoided emissions. It reads freight records for trips that move your scrap and places those lines in the Scope 3 evidence trail, so the Category 5 transport figure has a document behind it.
